annotationRationale: The method uses the product's sign and integer factor pairs to enumerate all candidates, then proves the minimum by comparing their sums and exhibiting an attaining triple.
sourceMethod: Follows the official enumeration of one positive and two negative factors. Adds a bound excluding positive factors at most 4 and organizes the complete enumeration in a table.

review.mathCheck: All-positive triples have sum at least 3. With two negatives, a positive sum requires p>a+b. For p≤4 the product is at most 36; the remaining divisor/factor-pair cases give sums −2, −1, 3, 5, 6, 10, 11, 16, 27, 58. Thus the minimum positive sum is 3, attained by (10,−1,−6), choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Solution 7 on page 4: exhibit sum 3 and exhaust signed factor triples. The added small-p bound makes completeness explicit.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed integer-enumeration and extremal-proof roles are appropriate; factor finding and product signs are supporting knowledge.
